From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and "[STANDARD]" labels.** These are the other side's assertions and are disregarded. Nothing in the Seller package has been "cleared by both sides" from the Buyer's perspective; we have no instruction from the Wattlebridge deal team that any point is agreed at principal level. The "market context" paragraph is Seller advocacy, not an agreed baseline. Every item below has been reviewed on its merits.

Baseline: 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap

- **Seller position:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 100% of price for all Claims, or at minimum 50% for general warranties, with fundamental, tax, specific indemnities and fraud outside the cap entirely.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%; counter at 100% (fallback 50%), with carve-outs. *Reason:* with a thin disclosure letter and live unresolved risks (Bluefen 30% of revenue, Riverlark, Ironquay, data incident), 20% leaves the Buyer materially under-protected.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

- **Seller position:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis ~AUD 10,000 (with related claims aggregated); basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%) on a tip-over/first-dollar basis; thresholds not to apply to fundamental warranties, tax, or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 10k / AUD 120k tipping basket, carve out fundamental/tax/indemnities. *Reason:* "excess only" plus a high de minimis could allow a series of real losses (e.g. the AUD 330k renewals, incident costs) to go largely unrecovered.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit

- **Seller position:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties (covering two audit cycles); 7 years for tax; 7 years/indefinite for fundamental; no cut-off for fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 18 months only as a fallback if other protections improve; otherwise 24 months, with separate longer periods for tax and fundamental. *Reason:* 18 months may expire before the first full post-Completion audit surfaces accounting or contract-level issues.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime

- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year claim period, no de minimis/basket, not qualified by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Firmly reject. *Reason:* a title defect is a failure of the entire bargain and "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery of the price at 20%.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out

- **Seller position:** No fraud carve-out appears; cl 12.3/9.3/12.8/20.5 say limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise, and the non-reliance language is unqualified.
- **Buyer should want:** Express carve-out of fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express carve-out as a non-negotiable. *Reason:* the absence of the carve-out is unusual even against Seller-friendly market norms, and the "all Claims" language would otherwise purport to limit fraud liability.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope

- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sched 7; DL 1.1–1.2), plus a blanket "no admission" clause (DL 1.4).
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure effective only to the extent "fairly disclosed" with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no general disclosure of public registers or a document-by-document data room dump; fundamental warranties and specific indemnities not qualified by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; require "fair disclosure" standard with specific disclosures against specific warranties; delete public-register disclosure. *Reason:* as drafted, every warranty is effectively qualified by anything buried in the data room, which neutralises the warranty package.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier

- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Delete cl 8.3 entirely; if any knowledge qualifier is accepted, limit to actual knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and excluding advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. *Reason:* "discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that converts the Buyer's own diligence into a shield for the Seller and overlaps with the already over-broad general disclosure.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent

- **Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** Bluefen consent (unconditional, or with conditions satisfied) as a hard Condition Precedent to Completion, with the Seller bearing the cost of any conditions; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; Buyer walk-right or price adjustment if not obtained by the long-stop date.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a true CP; do not accept "treat as satisfied on delivery" without the 11.3 conditions being met. *Reason:* Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; loss of that contract post-Completion would fundamentally change the value of the business.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility

- **Seller position:** AUD ~3.2m facility to be released "following Completion" (cl 2/7); DL 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Facility repaid out of Seller proceeds at Completion via the funds flow, with executed deed of release/discharge of security and PPSR release delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable; the AUD 3.2m treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require repayment and discharge at Completion, or escrow of the full amount. *Reason:* on a debt-free/cash-free deal the Buyer should never own a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a change-of-control default (cl 8.1) for even one day.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses

- **Seller position:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow; DL 5 confirms they are omitted and is silent on super, payroll tax and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and all on-costs treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the completion adjustment (or paid by the Seller through pre-Completion payroll with evidence), with a specific indemnity for any shortfall and clear allocation of who funds them when the continued-employment condition triggers post-Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Insert into the funds flow as a price deduction with gross-up for on-costs (estimate ~AUD 480–500k all-in) plus indemnity. *Reason:* these are triggered by the Seller's sale and will be paid by the Company post-Completion, so if unaddressed the Buyer funds them.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity

- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment and "adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every fee; AUD 180k open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:** Pre-Completion settlement of the AUD 180k by the Seller (or deduction), delivery of a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable, and a broad indemnity covering loss of title to or inability to use the SOW3 Project Materials (including re-development costs and third-party claims), uncapped or separately capped, not subject to basket/disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Expand indemnity and add confirmatory assignment as a CP/deliverable. *Reason:* if the fee is unpaid, the Company may not own core IP it has built into its product, and an indemnity sized to AUD 180k does not cover that exposure.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident

- **Seller position:** DD-006 is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sched 6); DL 6 confirms ~1,240 records, unknown access, unknown scope, notification question unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:** Seller to complete the investigation pre-Completion and provide findings; a specific indemnity (uncapped or capped at price, 6+ years, no basket, not qualified by disclosure) for all loss arising from the incident including OAIC notification/penalties, customer claims, remediation and contract terminations; a pre-Completion covenant to comply with the Privacy Act notification regime; warranty that no other incidents exist.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus investigation completion as a CP or Completion deliverable. *Reason:* an unresolved eligible-data-breach assessment carries regulatory, customer-contract (Bluefen/Mossvale) and reputational risk that the Seller cannot credibly characterise as immaterial while the facts are unknown.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals

- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs"; DL 8 does not say whether they are committed, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of the renewal terms; confirmation of whether they are committed pre-Completion; amounts accrued or committed but unpaid before Completion treated as Debt/working-capital in the completion adjustment; warranty that no renewals outside the ordinary course or on changed terms have been agreed; note DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together (timing/scope split suggests a possible structuring of a single AUD 330k commitment into three).
- **Recommendation:** Require disclosure of terms; treat committed-but-unpaid amounts in the price adjustment; add a specific warranty. *Reason:* three identical AUD 110k items split across two documents warrants verification before accepting the "ordinary course" label.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller position:** All limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes clearly drafted for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Riverlark), and (v) fraud – each with its own cap, threshold, time limit and disclosure treatment; "unless expressly stated otherwise" reversed so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12/13 into a schedule-based regime by Claim category. *Reason:* the current drafting collapses every protection into the weakest tier (20% cap / 18 months / disclosure-qualified / knowledge-qualified), which would gut the specific indemnities even if separately negotiated.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification

- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; DL 10 notes this is only the source relied on and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR search for security over the shares (particularly any Riverlark security), review of constitution for transfer restrictions/pre-emptive rights, review of any shareholder agreement/options/convertibles, and chain-of-title for any prior transfers; fundamental title warranties and a title indemnity at 100% of price.
- **Recommendation:** Complete ASIC/PPSR/constitution verification now; do not rely on the register alone. *Reason:* a company-maintained register is not conclusive and Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure, knowledge qualifier).
- **Buyer should want:** Full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax liabilities, uncapped or capped at price, 7-year period, no basket, not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge, with conduct-of-claims provisions); standalone IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments, open-source) with a longer period and a higher cap given this is a SaaS business, with the Ironquay matter carved out into its specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as OPEN and negotiate a separate tax indemnity and enhanced IP regime. *Reason:* for a software company, IP is the asset being bought, and tax exposure typically surfaces well beyond 18 months; neither belongs under the general cap.

---

## Summary of priority points for the mark-up

| Priority | Issue | Headline ask |
|---|---|---|
| Deal-critical | SPA-N-008 Bluefen | True CP with 11.3 conditions satisfied |
| Deal-critical | SPA-N-009 Riverlark | Repay/discharge at Completion, through funds flow |
| Deal-critical | SPA-N-005 Fraud | Express carve-out from all limitations |
| Deal-critical | SPA-N-004/014 Fundamental & category separation | Separate regimes; 100% cap on fundamental |
| Price-affecting | SPA-N-010 Bonuses | AUD 420k + on-costs as price deduction |
| Price-affecting | SPA-N-011 Ironquay | Pay AUD 180k pre-Completion + confirmatory assignment + broad indemnity |
| Price-affecting | SPA-N-012 Incident | Specific indemnity; complete investigation |
| Price-affecting | SPA-N-013 Sandbar | Disclose terms; adjust for committed amounts |
| Framework | SPA-N-006/007 Disclosure & knowledge | Fair disclosure standard; delete cl 8.3 |
| Framework | SPA-N-001/002/003 Cap/basket/time | 100% (fallback 50%); AUD 10k/120k tipping; 24 months |
| Diligence | SPA-N-015 Title | ASIC/PPSR/constitution checks now |
| Open | SPA-N-016 Tax/IP | Separate tax indemnity; enhanced IP regime |

The Seller's disclosure letter is, in places, more candid than the SPA update (it concedes that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment and the incident investigation are all incomplete). Those admissions should be used in the mark-up to justify the CPs and specific indemnities above.

- **Buyer should want:** Seller to complete the investigation pre-Completion and provide findings; a specific indemnity (uncapped or capped at price, 6+ years, no basket, not qualified by disclosure) for all loss arising from the incident including OAIC notification/penalties, customer claims, remediation and contract terminations; a pre-Completion covenant to comply with the Privacy Act notification regime; warranty that no other incidents exist.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus investigation completion as a CP or Completion deliverable. *Reason:* an unresolved eligible-data-breach assessment carries regulatory, customer-contract (Bluefen/Mossvale) and reputational risk that the Seller cannot credibly characterise as immaterial while the facts are unknown.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals

- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs"; DL 8 does not say whether they are committed, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of the renewal terms; confirmation of whether they are committed pre-Completion; amounts accrued or committed but unpaid before Completion treated as Debt/working-capital in the completion adjustment; warranty that no renewals outside the ordinary course or on changed terms have been agreed; note DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together (timing/scope split suggests a possible structuring of a single AUD 330k commitment into three).
- **Recommendation:** Require disclosure of terms; treat committed-but-unpaid amounts in the price adjustment; add a specific warranty. *Reason:* three identical AUD 110k items split across two documents warrants verification before accepting the "ordinary course" label.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller position:** All limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes clearly drafted for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Riverlark), and (v) fraud – each with its own cap, threshold, time limit and disclosure treatment; "unless expressly stated otherwise" reversed so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12/13 into a schedule-based regime by Claim category. *Reason:* the current drafting collapses every protection into the weakest tier (20% cap / 18 months / disclosure-qualified / knowledge-qualified), which would gut the specific indemnities even if separately negotiated.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification

- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; DL 10 notes this is only the source relied on and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR search for security over the shares (particularly any Riverlark security), review of constitution for transfer restrictions/pre-emptive rights, review of any shareholder agreement/options/convertibles, and chain-of-title for any prior transfers; fundamental title warranties and a title indemnity at 100% of price.
- **Recommendation:** Complete ASIC/PPSR/constitution verification now; do not rely on the register alone. *Reason:* a company-maintained register is not conclusive and Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure, knowledge qualifier).
- **Buyer should want:** Full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax liabilities, uncapped or capped at price, 7-year period, no basket, not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge, with conduct-of-claims provisions); standalone IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments, open-source) with a longer period and a higher cap given this is a SaaS business, with the Ironquay matter carved out into its specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as OPEN and negotiate a separate tax indemnity and enhanced IP regime. *Reason:* for a software company, IP is the asset being bought, and tax exposure typically surfaces well beyond 18 months; neither belongs under the general cap.
